## Outcome

Make the standard Windows runner validation reliable under parallel test execution without weakening production teardown/checkpoint safety or hiding failing assertions. Keep this separate from #211's native stopped-session evidence-access prerequisite.

## Observed September 9, 2026

At base 8198c4acdab1b119c00ab39d5353250781591631 plus the cfg(test)-only #211 diagnostic patch, `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace --target-dir target` reached the runner suite and returned **188 passed / 7 failed / 1 ignored**, in 166.33s. The 11 new #211 pure/wire tests pass. The seven failing test bodies and production lifecycle implementation are unchanged; `main.rs` only gains cfg(test) module registration. No baseline parallel control was run, so regression origin is not established.

Failures:
- `adapter::external::tests::claude_permission_bridge_denies_rejection_and_expiry`: approval-request timeout.
- `source_checkpoint::tests::issue190_cancelled_exit_checkpoints_before_terminal_event`: 0 checkpoint proofs instead of 1.
- `source_checkpoint::tests::issue190_cleanup_commit_rejects_a_late_retention_acknowledgment`: elapsed timeout.
- `source_checkpoint::tests::issue190_late_stop_cancels_held_ack_without_acceptance_or_post_verifier_seal`: elapsed timeout.
- `source_checkpoint::tests::issue190_stop_wins_over_provider_completion_and_seals_source`: 0 checkpoint proofs instead of 1.
- `source_checkpoint::tests::issue190_suspend_wins_over_provider_completion_and_seals_source`: 0 checkpoint proofs instead of 1.
- `tests::teardown_fail_closed_execute_assignment_preserves_exact_workspace_until_verified`: teardown uncertainty observation timed out.

Full output is retained in the owning QA evidence directory, `issue211-rust-final-20260909T191835097/workspace-tests.log`. The established #210 gate explicitly used `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` and `--test-threads=1`; that same serial workspace lane has now completed without changing these tests or timeout values: **458 passed / 0 failed / 276 ignored** overall, including **195 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored** in the runner (810.90s). The complete serial result is retained at `issue211-serial-workspace-20260909T192525276/workspace-tests.log`. This is not a green parallel-suite claim and does not establish causality.

## Acceptance

- Compare a bounded baseline/current run and identify fixture scheduling/resource contention versus an actual product lifecycle defect; do not guess causality from a retry.
- Keep exact source/policy/checkpoint/termination assertions and fail-closed behavior.
- Prefer owned, observed readiness/completion signals and bounded process resources over guessed sleeps or blanket timeout increases.
- Retain the original failure and exact local reproduction/outcomes; hosted Actions availability is not the gate.
- If serialization is the supported local contract, document and enforce it consistently in contributor commands while tracking any remaining parallel limitation explicitly.
- No real inference, production/app-DB mutation, or teardown of shared/manual services for a test-fixture investigation without its separate owned authorization.

This issue is curated follow-up work, not factory-ready and not a claim that a runtime defect is proven.

## Supplementary Windows fixture evidence from #79 / PR #307

The two connection fixtures in the [September 12 observation](https://github.com/All-The-Vibes/ecorp/issues/213#issuecomment-5644351739) also appeared in our #79 validation. Adding the environment classification here rather than opening a duplicate issue.

This is retained evidence from the #79 candidate, **not a fresh reproduction on current main**, not proof of the same cause as the earlier setup timeouts, and not acceptance evidence for closing #213.

- The earlier full-workspace run, before the final CLI selector correction, returned **517 passed / 36 failed / 329 ignored**.
- A bounded serial rerun of the 33 non-privilege-dependent runner failures used the actual runner test executable with a new, short, owned `TEMP`/`TMP` outside source checkouts: **31 passed / 2 failed / 0 ignored / 181 filtered out**.
- The 24 cases previously reporting path-length failures and seven other assertion failures passed in that diagnostic rerun. Changing the layout and execution conditions does not establish which factor caused the original failures or turn the full gate green.
- These two cases still failed, now reporting `private connection directory permissions could not be established`:
  - `connections::integration_tests::native_fixture_personal_github_profiles_and_login_replay_survive_restart`
  - `connections::integration_tests::native_fixture_ready_ack_refresh_rejection_and_old_run_pins_survive_restart`
- Three earlier Windows symlink-privilege cases were not rerun. Those three plus the two connection cases remain unverified on this host.

Environment: Windows, Rust 1.94.0 GNU, with the bundled Rust LLD configuration used for native execution. No elevation, Developer Mode, permission repair, global Git settings, OS-protection changes, or test-source/assertion changes were used for the bounded rerun. Failed fixtures were retained; no owned test processes or database/API listeners remained afterward.

[Published evidence, pinned to PR #307 commit 05e302c](https://github.com/All-The-Vibes/ecorp/blob/05e302c957b62611dcfde5583f11b659835f93cf/docs/evidence/2026-09-16-factory-cost-preflight.md#final-review-and-environment-follow-up).

Suggested diagnostic distinction: record the specific native-manager setup error, toolchain, fixture path, and permission capabilities before grouping these failures with scheduling timeouts. No request to weaken the private-directory checks, widen timeouts, or treat isolated passes as a release gate.

## Bounded investigation: timeout reproduced, no fix claimed

I completed the declared diagnostic pass at source `30ec3fab6acd566cc1fc1e574c8a6343d0ce0596`. No production change, timeout increase, skipped assertion, permission change or conjectural fixture fix was retained.

The two mixed-cohort invocations used the same source-bound diagnostic runner binary under default parallel scheduling:

- Initial layout: 49 passed / 26 failed. The long temporary root caused Git's `'$GIT_DIR' too big` fixture-setup failures. This is not a valid lifecycle-timing baseline.
- One shorter-root control: 73 passed / 2 failed. It reproduced `issue190_late_stop_cancels_held_ack_without_acceptance_or_post_verifier_seal` timing out after file-verifier evidence but before the deliverable-upload event. The other failure was a separate fixture-layout confound: the temporary root was inside a Git checkout, so the occupied-target test discovered the parent repository and failed its expected-error assertion.

The held-ACK trace observed adapter readiness, session termination and file-verifier evidence. It did not observe deliverable upload before the unchanged 15-second fixture deadline. No late-stop/cancellation assertions were reached in that case. This narrows the investigation to the pre-upload export phase; it does not establish a product lifecycle defect.

Up to 14 concurrent Git spans were observed in the instrumented workspace/setup helpers, but the separate deliverable-export Git helpers were not instrumented. Resource contention is therefore still a hypothesis, not a proven cause or a justification for adding a limiter.

The pass used one Cargo build, two provenance listings and two behavioral invocations. Temporary diagnostics were removed surgically; the branch is clean at the original source/tree. Failed fixtures, diagnostic patch, exact binary/hash, original failures and generation-aware process observations are retained privately. No process was terminated and no retained service, provider or application database was touched.

**#213 remains unresolved.** The next useful experiment requires per-operation export timing and a short fixture root outside ambient Git discovery, followed by a matched comparison. The separate Windows symlink-privilege failures remain explicit. No green full-runner/workspace gate, commit, PR or closure is claimed.
